latest_nl_proof:
Fix n at least 2 and a sign sequence s=(s_1,...,s_{n-1}) with each s_i in {+1,-1}. Let A_s be the set of permutations a=(a_1,...,a_n) of {1,...,n} such that s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i)>0 for every i=1,...,n-1. By definition, |A_s|=f(s). Similarly define A_{-s}.

Define a map T on permutations of {1,...,n} by
T(a_1,...,a_n)=(n+1-a_1,...,n+1-a_n).
Because the map x -> n+1-x is a bijection from {1,...,n} to itself, T sends permutations of {1,...,n} to permutations of {1,...,n}. Also T is an involution, since applying it twice gives back the original permutation:
T(T(a_1,...,a_n))=(a_1,...,a_n).
Hence T is a bijection on the set of all permutations of {1,...,n}.

Now take any a=(a_1,...,a_n) in A_s, and write b=T(a). For each i=1,...,n-1 we have
b_{i+1}-b_i=(n+1-a_{i+1})-(n+1-a_i)=-(a_{i+1}-a_i).
Therefore
(-s_i)(b_{i+1}-b_i)=(-s_i)(-(a_{i+1}-a_i))=s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i)>0.
So b satisfies the defining inequalities for A_{-s}, and thus T(a) is in A_{-s}.

Conversely, if b is in A_{-s}, the same calculation applied to T(b) shows that T(b) is in A_s, because T is its own inverse. Therefore T restricts to a bijection from A_s onto A_{-s}.

Since bijective finite sets have the same cardinality, |A_s|=|A_{-s}|. Equivalently, f(s)=f(-s). This is exactly the claimed statement.
role_in_parent: This symmetry reduces the analysis of patterns starting with -1 to the already solved case of patterns starting with +1, and it also shows the two alternating maximizers have equal value.
statement_nl: Let n be an integer at least 2, and let s=(s_1,...,s_{n-1}) with each s_i in {+1,-1}. Define -s=(-s_1,...,-s_{n-1}). Let f(s) be the number of permutations a=(a_1,...,a_n) of {1,...,n} such that s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i)>0 for every 1 <= i <= n-1. Then f(s)=f(-s).

domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n is at least 2
s has exactly n minus 1 components
Each component of s is either plus 1 or minus 1
The negated sequence -s is formed entry by entry
a is a permutation of the integers from 1 through n
The inequality is strict: the product must be greater than 0 for every index i from 1 to n minus 1
The index i ranges over all integers from 1 to n minus 1
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer n at least 2 and every sign sequence s of length n minus 1, the number of permutations a of 1 through n for which each adjacent difference has the sign prescribed by s is equal to the number of permutations counted using the coordinatewise negated sign sequence -s.
quantifier_order: For every integer n at least 2
For every sign sequence s of length n minus 1 with entries plus 1 or minus 1
For the count defining f(s), consider all permutations a of 1 through n
For each index i from 1 to n minus 1, require that the i-th sign times the difference between the next two entries of a is positive

variables.domain: sequences of length n minus 1 with each entry equal to plus 1 or minus 1
variables.name: s
variables.role: input parameter for the counting function

variables.domain: ordered n-tuples whose entries are exactly the integers from 1 through n, each used once
variables.name: a

witness_dependencies: No existential witnesses appear in the statement; the only object being quantified over inside the definition of f(s) is the counted permutation a.
